C-SYSTEMONE-DECISION-BACKEND.IntentSummary: Add a provider-neutral System One decision client for the de-facto POST /v1/systemone protocol (noul, choice, score) selected by baseUrl and model, add an optional strict canonical systemone connection section plus a systemone plugin toggle, and add guardian.decisionBackend ("fast" | "systemone") with an explicit shadow-calibration mode and fail-closed fallback to the existing fast auxiliary path, keeping the fast backend the default and shipping no implicit hosted endpoint.

PlanningNotes.Note: Measured on the reference host before edits: bun run check 89s, bun run build 18s, bun run pack:check 29s; budgets are ordinary leaf gates and the runner default applies. The isolated live-host contract gate is not part of this change.

Optional live smoke against a real System One endpoint is a manual developer step using a short-lived key from the environment; it is never a repository or CI gate and no key or endpoint is committed.

Scope is deliberately one consumer: the added client is provider-neutral and Guardian is the only caller. OpenAI Decisions API and Qwen/Alibaba decision adapters are deferred until a public schema exists, and every other System One use case (context pruning, reviewer triage, semantic spec lint, routing, screening) is a separate future change.

Fail-closed rule: any disabled, unconfigured, unreachable, timed-out, or malformed provider outcome makes Guardian defer to manual approval through the existing fast path; the provider never becomes an acceptance or review authority.

T-001.Title: Provider-neutral System One client: request shaping, typed noul/choice/score decoding, bounded transport

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: systemone.ts posts {model, state, questions} to {baseUrl}/v1/systemone over an injectable transport, decodes noul as a 0..1 probability, choice as a winning key with per-option probabilities and confidence, and score as an interpolated value with per-level probabilities and confidence, and ignores unknown response fields and provider-specific extras.
The client is vendor-neutral: it contains no jev-, typesafe-, or other vendor-specific field or branch, and any compliant endpoint is reached by baseUrl and model alone.
The client applies the configured request timeout and a bounded retry count, never retries unboundedly, and surfaces a typed, credential-safe error that never includes the apiKey or the raw state.

Tests use an injected transport and cover request shaping, each answer type, unknown-field tolerance, timeout, retry bound, and credential-safe error text; no live endpoint, key, or network call is used.

T-002.Title: Canonical config: optional systemone section, guardian decisionBackend, strict schema v3 widening

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: vvoc-config.ts adds a SystemOneConfig type and createSystemOneConfig defaulting enabled true, timeoutMs and maxRetries, requiring non-empty baseUrl and model when the section is present, accepting an optional ${VAR} apiKey, and clearing unknown keys.

guardian config gains decisionBackend ("fast" | "systemone", default "fast") and an optional nested systemone object with shadow (boolean, default false) and lowRiskThreshold (0..1, default 0.95); createGuardianConfig seeds them conservatively so existing documents keep validating.

schemas/vvoc/v3.json gains the optional systemone property and the guardian decisionBackend and systemone properties, the embedded schema stays byte-equal to schemas/vvoc/v3.json, and a previously valid v3 document still validates.
Tests cover parse, render, defaults, rejection of missing baseUrl or model, invalid decisionBackend and threshold values, and continued validity of a pre-change document.

T-003.Title: System One plugin toggle: canonical name, default entry, conservative materialization

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: plugin-toggle-config.ts adds "systemone" to PLUGIN_TOGGLE_NAMES and a default enabled entry materialized into vvoc.json on sync/init without overwriting any user-set value.
The toggle is resolvable through the shared isPluginEnabled helper, and an existing v3 document without the key remains enabled by default.
Tests cover the new canonical name, default value, materialization conservatism, and that a user-provided boolean or object entry wins.

T-004.Title: Guardian backend switch: systemone assessment, shadow calibration, fail-closed fallback

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Guardian keeps the fast backend as its default and produces identical decisions when decisionBackend is "fast", proven by the existing Guardian scenarios passing unchanged.

With decisionBackend "systemone", Guardian builds the provider state from the existing bounded review input and derives the assessment from a noul low-risk question and a score risk rubric, mapping to risk_level and risk_score and reusing the existing low-and-below-threshold auto-approval rule.

With shadow enabled, the systemone provider is evaluated and a structured comparison is logged, but the permission effect is decided solely by the fast backend and is never mutated by the observed systemone answer.

When the provider is disabled, unconfigured, unavailable, timed out, or returns a missing or malformed noul or score, Guardian defers to manual approval and never auto-approves, and no error escapes the permission hook.
The systemone plugin toggle off constructs no provider and forces the fast backend.

Tests use the injectable Guardian inference seam and an injected systemone transport, and cover fast parity, systemone allow and defer, shadow non-mutation, unset key, provider failure, toggle off, and key absence from logs.

T-005.Title: Durable state and docs: graph, verification, README

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: .grace/graph/main.xml gains M-SYSTEMONE-PROVIDER describing the provider-neutral client, and updates M-PLUGIN-GUARDIAN, M-CLI-CONFIG, and M-PLUGIN-TOGGLE-CONFIG to reflect the decisionBackend, systemone section, and toggle.
.grace/verification/main.xml gains V-M-SYSTEMONE-PROVIDER and updates V-M-PLUGIN-GUARDIAN, V-M-CLI-CONFIG, and V-M-PLUGIN-TOGGLE-CONFIG with the new test files and commands.

README documents the systemone section, the guardian decisionBackend and shadow mode, the fast default, the vendor-neutral baseUrl and model selection, key handling, and that no hosted endpoint is assumed.

T-006.Title: Full verification gate: check, build, packaging

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Fresh evidence passes: bun run check (typecheck, lint, format, GRACE markup, tool contracts, all tests), bun run build, and bun run pack:check, each within its declared budget.

The change final GRACE gate is run externally after observed writes: grace lint --path . --change C-SYSTEMONE-DECISION-BACKEND --assertions final with run-commands, and no GRACE lifecycle command is nested inside a plan assertion.

Verification.Command: bun run check && bun run build && bun run pack:check
